SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: USE OF MEDICINE
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Use of medicine helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: USE OF MEDICINE
Study Use of medicine like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of medicine” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Use of medicine matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Use of medicine in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Use of medicine in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Use of medicine in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Use of medicine this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Use of medicine in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Use of medicine in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Use of medicine in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Use of medicine in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of medicine” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Use of medicine in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Use of medicine is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of medicine” around your school. (skill: explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Use of medicine matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Use of medicine this week. (skill: practise Use of medicine in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Use of medicine” around your school. (skill: apply Use of medicine in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Use of medicine to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Use of medicine in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Use of medicine from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Use of medicine: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Use of medicine?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

1. Know what Use of medicine means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Use of medicine means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Use of medicine from Kenya.
